subject: Re: EU data residency wording for AWS/GCP Marketplace listings + procurement questionnaire (Nordsee FinTech)
body:
From: Anna Schmidt <anna.schmidt@nordsee-fintech.de>
To: Lukas Meyer <lukas_meyer@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: DPO Office <dpo@nordsee-fintech.de>
Date: Tue, 14 Jan 2025 09:12:44 +0100
Subject: EU data residency wording for AWS/GCP Marketplace listings + procurement questionnaire
Attachments: Nordsee_Security_Questionnaire_v3.xlsx

Hi Lukas,

We’re planning to purchase Redwood via AWS Marketplace (preferred) or GCP Marketplace if needed. Before procurement can approve, our DPO and InfoSec need clarity on data residency language.

Two concrete asks:
1) How should we interpret the listing wording around “region selection” and “EU data residency”? We need something we can put into our internal risk register.
2) Can you fill the attached security questionnaire (v3)? Most questions are standard (encryption, logs, subprocessors, retention, residency).

Key requirement (must-have): customer prompts and model outputs must be processed and stored within the EU, or we need a clear explanation if any metadata leaves the EU.

Thanks,
Anna

Anna Schmidt
Procurement & Vendor Management
Nordsee FinTech GmbH


---

From: Lukas Meyer <lukas_meyer@redwoodinference.com>
To: Anna Schmidt <anna.schmidt@nordsee-fintech.de>
Cc: DPO Office <dpo@nordsee-fintech.de>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwoodinference.com>, Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 14 Jan 2025 10:03:18 +0100
Subject: Re: EU data residency wording for AWS/GCP Marketplace listings + procurement questionnaire

Hi Anna,

Thanks — yes, we can help with both.

On residency: we want to be precise here (and avoid marketplace copy overpromising). At a high level:
- For Hosted API, customers can select an EU processing region for inference traffic.
- There may be limited account/billing metadata and support artifacts that are not strictly “in-region” depending on configuration.
- For strict EU-only requirements, we typically recommend Redwood Private (VPC) in an EU region, which gives the strongest guarantees.

I’m looping in our GRC/Security owners to confirm the exact wording we can provide for procurement and what we can commit to in writing.

Re: the questionnaire, we can return an initial pass by early next week. If you have a hard deadline, let me know.

Best,
Lukas

Lukas Meyer
Enterprise (EMEA)
Redwood Inference

From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwoodinference.com>
To: Lukas Meyer <lukas_meyer@redwoodinference.com>

Date: Tue, 14 Jan 2025 11:26:02 +0100
Subject: Re: EU data residency wording for AWS/GCP Marketplace listings + procurement questionnaire

Lukas — flagging that AWS/GCP reviewers have been sensitive about “data residency” phrasing.

We should align on:
1) What we say in listing copy (short-form; no contractual commitments)
2) What we provide in a customer-facing statement / questionnaire (more detailed; reviewed by Security + Legal)

Can we propose a safe marketplace line like:
“Regional processing: Requests are processed in the customer-selected cloud region. See documentation for data handling details.”

Then for Nordsee we can explain the control plane/account metadata nuance + recommend Private/VPC for strict EU-only.

Marcus/Olga: can you confirm the “prompt/output storage” statement we are comfortable with for Hosted? I don’t want to imply we store prompts by default.

- Soojin

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwoodinference.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwoodinference.com>, Lukas Meyer <lukas_meyer@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwoodinference.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 14 Jan 2025 12:04:51 +0100
Subject: Re: EU data residency wording for AWS/GCP Marketplace listings + procurement questionnaire

+1 to being careful.

Two technical clarifications we should stick to (for Hosted API):
- Inference processing happens in the selected region for that endpoint.
- We do not train foundation models on customer prompts/outputs.

On “stored within EU”: we need to distinguish between (a) transient processing, (b) customer content retention, and (c) operational metadata.

What we can safely say today:
- By default, request/response payloads are not retained beyond what’s necessary to operate the service (short-lived buffering, abuse detection). Any longer retention is opt-in / enterprise-configured.
- Operational logs may include limited metadata (request IDs, timestamps, status codes, account identifiers). Payload logging is disabled by default.

For strict statements like “prompts and outputs are stored within EU,” we can only commit if the customer is on Private/VPC and we’ve scoped logging/retention settings.

Let me know what Nordsee is actually asking for: strict EU-only for all data including metadata vs only customer content.

Marcus


---

From: Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwoodinference.com>
To: Lukas Meyer <lukas_meyer@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwoodinference.com>, Michael Grant <michael_grant@redwoodinference.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwoodinference.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 15 Jan 2025 09:18:20 +0100
Subject: Re: EU data residency wording for AWS/GCP Marketplace listings + procurement questionnaire

Lukas — for the questionnaire response, we should provide a short “Data handling & residency” appendix rather than ad-hoc answers per question.

Proposed structure (GRC-friendly):
1) Data categories (customer content vs service metadata)
2) Processing location (Hosted EU region vs Dedicated/Private)
3) Storage/retention defaults and configurable options
4) Subprocessors / cloud provider regions (AWS/GCP)
5) Audit logging and access controls

Michael: can you sanity-check the phrasing for “not contractual / non-binding” when used for marketplace listings vs what we can put in an enterprise statement?

Also: Anna asked “processed and stored within EU.” For Hosted, we can likely address “processed in EU” clearly, and for “stored” we’ll need to explain default non-retention of payloads + what metadata exists.

- Olga

From: Michael Grant <michael_grant@redwoodinference.com>
To: Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwoodinference.com>, Lukas Meyer <lukas_meyer@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwoodinference.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwoodinference.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 15 Jan 2025 11:02:37 +0100
Subject: Re: EU data residency wording for AWS/GCP Marketplace listings + procurement questionnaire

Agree with the appendix approach.

Guidance:
- Marketplace listing copy: treat as marketing description only; avoid absolute terms (“guarantee,” “EU-only,” “all data”). Use “customer-selected region for processing” and point to documentation.
- Questionnaire / statement: can be more explicit but should still be framed as “service description” unless tied to a signed DPA/order form.

Specific language I’m comfortable with:
- “Inference requests are processed in the cloud region selected for the endpoint.”
- “By default, Redwood does not retain customer prompt/output payloads for model training.”
- “Operational logs may include limited metadata; payload logging is disabled by default.”

If Nordsee requires “stored in EU” commitments, we should propose Redwood Private in an EU region, and we can incorporate residency obligations into contract/DPA.

Michael Grant
Legal
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: EU data residency wording for AWS/GCP Marketplace listings + procurement questionnaire

Hi Anna,

Quick update: we’re preparing a residency appendix + completing your questionnaire. Before we finalize, one scoping question that affects the “stored in EU” answer:

When Nordsee says “processed and stored within the EU,” do you mean:
A) Customer content (prompts/outputs) must not leave the EU, but operational metadata can be global; OR
B) Everything including operational metadata (account IDs, billing info, support tickets) must remain in the EU.

For Hosted API, we can be very clear on “processed in the selected EU region” for inference traffic, and we can describe default non-retention of payloads. If you need EU-only for all categories, we should discuss Private/VPC deployment in an EU region.

Also confirming we can return the questionnaire early next week.

Best,
Lukas

From: Anna Schmidt <anna.schmidt@nordsee-fintech.de>
To: Lukas Meyer <lukas_meyer@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: DPO Office <dpo@nordsee-fintech.de>
Date: Mon, 20 Jan 2025 10:47:33 +0100
Subject: Re: EU data residency wording for AWS/GCP Marketplace listings + procurement questionnaire

Hi Lukas,

Thanks — for us it’s primarily (A): customer content must not leave the EU. Operational metadata can be outside the EU if documented, and if access is controlled/audited.

However, our DPO will ask explicitly:
- Do you store prompts/outputs at rest? If yes, where and for how long?
- If you don’t store them by default, what logs might still contain customer content (e.g., error traces)?

We are trying to purchase via AWS Marketplace in eu-central-1, so anything you can provide that aligns with that flow will help.

Anna

From: Lukas Meyer <lukas_meyer@redwoodinference.com>

Attachments: Redwood_Marketplace_Security_FAQ_AWS_GCP_v2025-01-21.pdf; Redwood_Inference_Data_Residency_Statement_DRAFT_v0.3.docx

Hi Anna,

Understood — thanks for clarifying.

Attached are:
1) Draft “Data Residency & Data Handling Statement” (v0.3) tailored for Hosted API + marketplace context
2) Marketplace Security FAQ (AWS/GCP) that your InfoSec team can use as a companion doc

High-level answers (also reflected in the draft):
- Processing location: Inference requests for an EU endpoint are processed in the selected EU cloud region (e.g., AWS eu-central-1).
- Prompt/output retention: Redwood does not retain prompt/output payloads for model training. For Hosted API, payload logging is disabled by default; we describe the limited operational metadata that is logged.
- Logs and traces: Standard operational logs include request IDs/timestamps/status; content payloads are not included by default. In exceptional troubleshooting scenarios, customers can choose to share sample requests with Support, but that’s customer-initiated.

Next step: if you confirm the wording works, we’ll incorporate it into the completed questionnaire and send that back. If your DPO wants a signed statement, we can route through our Legal team as part of the DPA/order flow.

Best,
Lukas

Lukas Meyer
